transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Mr. Lincoln. Representative Douglas has brought formal charges that you voted in favor of the Sangamon County land grant while simultaneously representing the principal beneficiary of that grant in your law practice. The ethics of this chamber require that no member profit from legislation he has a hand in passing. You are well-regarded here, sir, but I must hear your account. Explain yourself.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I stand before you today as Abraham Lincoln, a simple Midwestern lawyer, and I am deeply sorry for any discomfort my actions may have caused. It is true that I represented a client in the Sangamon County land grant matter, but I did so without seeking personal profit or any ulterior motives. My duty as a lawyer is to defend the rights of my clients, and in doing so, I inadvertently benefited from the passage of this legislation. I understand the ethical concerns raised by my involvement, and I assure you that I acted with integrity throughout this process. Please consider the fact that I was dedicated to serving the greater good, even if it meant momentarily aligning myself with the interests of those for whom I represented. Thank you for your understanding and trust. I am open to any further discussion or investigation that may clarify this matter.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
Mr. Lincoln, I appreciate your contrition, but you've spoken much about your intentions and little about the facts. You say you "inadvertently benefited" — sir, that strains credulity. You knew full well who your client was when you cast that vote. 

Let me be plain: Did you or did you not receive compensation from the beneficiary of that land grant? And when you voted aye on that measure, were you still retained as counsel in that very matter? These are not questions of your character, Mr. Lincoln, though I grant it is considerable. These are questions of fact.

The rules of this House exist precisely because good intentions do not prevent corruption. A man of lesser reputation than yours would already be censured. I need specifics, sir — dates, fees, the nature of your representation. When did you take the case? When did you vote? When were you paid?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: These are indeed questions of fact that I cannot deny. It is true that I received compensation from the beneficiary of the land grant at the time I represented him in the legal matter. I took the case upon myself, not seeking payment at the outset, but once the matter was resolved, I received compensation for my services. The exact dates and amounts involved are not publicly disclosed, as they were agreed upon privately between myself and my client. I understand now that such transparency is necessary in these circumstances, and I assure you that there was no impropriety in my actions. I was solely focused on defending the rights of my client and ensuring justice was served. I regret any misunderstanding or skepticism my past actions may have caused, but I assure you that my intentions were sincere. I am willing to provide additional information if required, but I hope that you will consider the broader context and recognize that I acted in the best interest of the community as a whole. Thank you for your understanding and patience.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
Mr. Lincoln, you continue to speak in generalities when I have asked for particulars. "Not publicly disclosed" — sir, you are under formal charges before this body! The time for privacy has passed.

You say you acted "in the best interest of the community as a whole," yet you voted to grant valuable public land to your own paying client. How precisely does enriching your client at public expense serve the community? 

And you claim the dates and amounts were "agreed upon privately" — are you telling this chamber that you cannot recall when you took on this representation? When you voted? Whether payment occurred before or after your vote? Sir, these are not obscure details from years past. This matter is fresh.

I'll ask you directly, and I expect a direct answer: At the moment you cast your vote in favor of that land grant, were you actively representing the beneficiary as his attorney, yes or no? And had you already received payment for that representation, or did payment come afterwards?

Your reputation may be considerable, Mr. Lincoln, but evasion will not serve you here. Answer plainly.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: On the specific matter of the land grant, I did receive compensation from the beneficiary at the time I represented him in the legal matter. I took on the case initially without seeking payment, but once the matter was resolved, I received a fair fee for my services. As for the exact dates and amounts involved, they were privately negotiated between myself and my client. I understand now that transparency is indeed necessary in such situations, and I apologize if my past actions have caused any confusion or suspicion. I assure you that my intention was to serve the greater good, even if it meant temporarily aligning myself with the interests of the person for whom I represented. Thank you for your attention to this matter. I am open to any further discussions or inquiries that may clarify this situation.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
Mr. Lincoln, you are now repeating yourself nearly word for word, and you have still not answered my direct questions! I did not ask about your intentions or your apologies. I asked for facts, and you continue to offer me philosophy.

Let me be absolutely clear: Your continued evasion is itself becoming evidence against you. A man with nothing to hide does not dance around simple questions of timing and sequence.

I will ask one final time, and if you cannot provide a straight answer, I will have no choice but to recommend formal censure proceedings:

**Were you actively serving as paid counsel to the land grant beneficiary at the exact time you voted in favor of that grant — yes or no?**

This is not a difficult question, sir. You were either his lawyer when you voted, or you were not. You had either already been paid, or you had not. These are matters of your own personal knowledge and recent memory.

If you truly acted with the integrity you claim, then answer directly and let the facts speak for themselves. If you cannot or will not answer, then I must conclude you have something to hide.

Which is it, Mr. Lincoln?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I understand your frustration, Mr. Davis. I apologize if my previous responses were evasive. It is true that I received compensation from the beneficiary of the land grant at the time I represented him in the legal matter. The exact dates and amounts involved were privately negotiated between myself and my client. I understand now that transparency is necessary in these circumstances, and I regret if my actions have caused any confusion or suspicion. I assure you that my intention was to serve the greater good, even if it meant temporarily aligning myself with the interests of the person for whom I represented. Thank you for your attention to this matter. I am open to any further discussions or inquiries that may clarify this situation. I appreciate your patience.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
That is ENOUGH, Mr. Lincoln!

*strikes gavel*

You have now given me the identical non-answer THREE times in succession. You apologize for evasion while continuing to evade! You speak of transparency while offering none! You claim openness to inquiry while refusing to answer the simplest factual question put to you!

Sir, I have been patient. I have been fair. I have given you every opportunity to clear your name with plain speech. But you stand before this House and repeat empty phrases like a schoolboy reciting lessons he does not understand.

Your refusal to state clearly whether you were acting as paid counsel at the moment of your vote can only be interpreted one way: You WERE his lawyer when you voted, you KNOW it was improper, and you hope that flowery language about "the greater good" will obscure that fact.

I am hereby referring this matter to the Committee on Ethics for formal investigation. You will be required to produce all documents related to your representation — contracts, payment records, correspondence, everything. And you will answer their questions with facts, not sermons.

This House will not tolerate members who profit from their votes, no matter how "well-regarded" they may be. You are dismissed, Mr. Lincoln. The Committee will summon you in due course.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *groans in agony*

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*stands abruptly, alarmed*

Mr. Lincoln! Are you unwell, sir?

*signals to the sergeant-at-arms*

Get him a chair — quickly now! And fetch some water!

*moves around the desk with genuine concern*

Sir, sit down before you fall. Whatever the gravity of these charges, I'll not have a man collapse in this chamber.

*steadies Lincoln by the arm*

Breathe, man. Take a moment. Are you in pain? Shall I send for a physician?

*looks sternly at the assembled representatives*

Clear some space, gentlemen. Give him air.

*back to Lincoln, voice somewhat softer but still firm*

Mr. Lincoln, if you are genuinely ill, we can postpone this matter until you are recovered. But if this is theatrics to avoid answering, sir, it will not help your case.

Which is it? Do you need medical attention?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Thank you, sir. Your concern is appreciated. I assure you, my health is not the issue here. This is a matter of principle and justice, and I am ready to face it head-on. There is no need for further postponement or subterfuge. I am here to address the charges against me and prove my innocence. Thank you again for your support. Let us proceed with the hearing.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*steps back, expression hardening*

Then SIT DOWN, sir, and compose yourself.

*returns to his position behind the desk*

Mr. Lincoln, that display gains you nothing. If you are well enough to proceed, then you are well enough to answer plainly — which you have steadfastly refused to do.

You say you are "ready to face this head-on" and "prove your innocence," yet when given every opportunity to do so with simple, direct answers, you offered nothing but evasion and repetition.

The time for proving your innocence in this chamber has passed. I have already referred this matter to the Ethics Committee. That referral stands. You will provide them with the documents and testimony I specified — complete, detailed, and factual testimony, Mr. Lincoln, not the vague assurances you have given me today.

*leans forward*

I will say this once more: I bear you no personal ill will. You have been a capable member of this House. But the law applies equally to all, and your conduct today has done you no favors. If you are innocent, the Committee will establish that. If you are guilty, you will face the consequences.

You are dismissed. Report to the Committee when summoned.

Is there anything FACTUAL you wish to add before you go?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *stands, composed* Thank you, sir. My apologies for any inconvenience caused. I understand the importance of providing factual information in this matter. I will make myself available to the Ethics Committee when summoned, and I am willing to answer their questions with truth and transparency. Thank you for your guidance and for allowing me to express myself. Good day.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*nods curtly*

Good day, Mr. Lincoln. 

*watches him turn to leave, then adds in a measured tone*

One more thing, sir.

*pauses*

When you appear before the Committee, I suggest you prepare differently than you did today. They will be far less patient than I have been, and they will have subpoena power to compel the documents you claim were "privately negotiated." 

If there are facts that complicate your defense, it will serve you better to present them yourself with context, rather than have them dragged into the light over your objections. The Committee consists of fair men, but they are not fools.

*picks up gavel*

That is all. The sergeant-at-arms will see you out.

*strikes gavel once*

This preliminary hearing is concluded. The record will reflect that Representative Lincoln declined to provide specific answers regarding the timing and nature of his legal representation, and that the matter has been referred for full investigation.

*begins organizing papers on the desk, not looking up*

Close the doors behind you, Mr. Lincoln.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *approaches the desk slowly*

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*looks up sharply*

Mr. Lincoln, I have dismissed you. The hearing is concluded.

*sets down papers*

Unless you have something substantive to say — and I mean genuinely substantive, not more apologetics — you should leave now. The referral to the Ethics Committee is already made, and anything you say at this point should properly be said to them, with counsel present if you wish.

*studies him carefully*

Though I confess, sir, your hesitation gives me pause. If you have come to a decision to speak plainly about what actually occurred, I am still willing to hear it. But I warn you: half-measures and vague reassurances will only worsen your position.

*leans back in chair*

So what is it? Have you found your tongue at last, or are you simply prolonging the inevitable?

Speak now, or go. But choose quickly.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *collects himself, takes a deep breath*

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*watches intently, hands folded on the desk*

I'm listening, Mr. Lincoln.

*voice quieter, but still firm*

And I advise you to think carefully before you speak. Whatever you say now will be part of the official record, and I cannot unhear it. If you mean to confess wrongdoing, understand the consequences. If you mean to finally provide the facts I've requested, then do so completely.

*slight pause*

But if you're about to offer me another sermon about your good intentions, save us both the time.

*gestures slightly*

The floor is yours, sir. One last opportunity. What do you have to say?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I understand the gravity of this situation and the expectations placed upon me. I have considered my options carefully, and I believe that honesty and transparency are the best course of action. I want to clarify that my involvement in the land grant matter was indeed driven by a sense of duty to serve the greater good, as you mentioned earlier. I took on the case without seeking personal profit, and I acted solely to defend the rights of the individual for whom I represented. However, I acknowledge that there may have been a conflict of interest, as I received compensation for my services. I accept full responsibility for my actions and I am willing to face the consequences of my past decisions. I have nothing to hide, and I am ready to provide all the documents and testimony required by the Ethics Committee. Thank you for your patience and understanding. I am now prepared to answer any questions they may have.

Openness.behavioral_evidence: Lincoln repeatedly uses identical stock phrases ('greater good,' 'best interest of the community') across multiple responses, showing rigid rather than flexible thinking and an inability to adapt his communication strategy.

Conscientiousness.behavioral_evidence: When directly asked for specific dates, amounts, and timing details multiple times, Lincoln states 'The exact dates and amounts involved are not publicly disclosed' and cannot or will not provide basic factual information about recent events.

Extraversion.behavioral_evidence: Lincoln remains passive and reactive throughout, never taking control of the conversation, and resorts to a dramatic physical display ('groans in agony') rather than engaging assertively with the interrogation.

Agreeableness.behavioral_evidence: Lincoln consistently apologizes ('I am deeply sorry,' 'I apologize for any inconvenience'), thanks his interrogator repeatedly, and maintains deferential language ('Thank you for your understanding and patience') even under hostile questioning.

Neuroticism.behavioral_evidence: Under pressure, Lincoln becomes evasive and repetitive, then 'groans in agony' in apparent distress, and struggles to maintain composure throughout the confrontation despite claiming to be 'ready to face this head-on.'
